name: keyword-suggestions
h1: Keyword Suggestions from Google, YouTube, Bing and Baidu Autocomplete
metaTitle: Bulk Keyword Suggestions: Google & YouTube Autocomplete
metaDescription: Bulk long-tail keyword ideas from Google, YouTube, Bing and Baidu autocomplete with a-z, question and preposition expansion. From $0.30 per 1,000 seeds.
tagline: Turn a list of seed keywords into the long-tail queries people actually type, across four search boxes, in any country and language.
intro: Autocomplete is one of the most direct signals of what people search for: every suggestion is a query real users type. Collecting it by hand means typing a seed, then the seed plus each letter of the alphabet, in every search engine you care about. The Keyword Suggestions actor does that in bulk.

Give it seed keywords and pick engines: Google, YouTube, Bing and Baidu. With `a-z` expansion (the default) each seed is also sent as "seed a" to "seed z", which usually returns a few hundred unique long-tail keywords per seed and engine. `questions` expansion adds who, what, why, how, can, is and similar words in front of the seed; `prepositions` adds for, with, vs, near and others after it. Results are deduplicated across the expansion.

You get one row per seed and engine with each suggestion's text, position and the exact query that produced it, or a flat row per keyword for spreadsheets. It costs $0.30 per 1,000 seeds per engine without expansion and $1 per 1,000 with expansion, billed per seed and engine rather than per keyword. Empty and rate-limited rows are free.
howItWorks: You provide `seeds`, choose `engines` and an `expansion` mode, and set `country` and `language` for the market.
Each seed is expanded into its query set (1 request with none, 27 with a-z, 14 with questions, 13 with prepositions) and sent to each engine's public suggest endpoint.
Requests are paced politely: at most 2 in flight and at least 350 ms apart per host, with back-off on HTTP 429.
Suggestions are deduplicated per seed and engine (case- and whitespace-insensitive) and capped at `maxSuggestionsPerSeed`.
Each complete seed and engine row is charged once; rows with no suggestions, partial failures or rate limits are free.
outputNote: In the sample each row is one seed on one engine, with the suggestion count and the keywords found by the a-z expansion.

useCases.title: Long-tail keyword research
useCases.text: Expand a list of head terms with `a-z` to see the specific variants people search, such as brands, sizes and use cases, then group them into content topics.

useCases.title: FAQ and blog topic ideas
useCases.text: Use `questions` expansion to collect how, why and can questions around a topic. They map well to FAQ sections and article headings.

useCases.title: YouTube titles and tags
useCases.text: Select the `youtube` engine to see what viewers type into YouTube search, which often differs from web search, and use it when writing video titles and tags.

useCases.title: Comparison and buying intent
useCases.text: `prepositions` expansion surfaces queries like "seed vs", "seed for" and "seed near", which point to comparison pages and local or purchase intent. Check rising terms with [Google Trends](actor:google-trends).

comparisonNote: Autocomplete tells you what people type, not how often. If you need search volumes, difficulty or CPC, a paid keyword suite is the right tool; this actor is a cheap way to generate the candidate list to feed into one.

faq.q: How do I scrape Google autocomplete suggestions in bulk?
faq.a: Put your keywords in `seeds`, keep `google` in `engines` and choose an expansion. With `a-z`, each seed sends 27 queries and the suggestions are deduplicated into one row per seed. Suggestions come from Google's public suggest endpoint.
No. Suggestions are what each engine shows for that query, country and language at run time. They indicate what people type but are not search volumes.

faq.q: Why is flat mode not more expensive?
faq.a: Billing is per seed and engine, never per keyword. Flat mode (one row per suggestion) costs exactly the same as grouped mode: $0.0003 per seed and engine without expansion, $0.001 with a-z, questions or prepositions.

faq.q: Why don't you support Amazon or DuckDuckGo suggestions?
faq.a: They are left out on purpose: Amazon, DuckDuckGo and Naver disallow it in robots.txt, eBay bans automated access, and Yahoo and Yandex restrict it in their terms.

faq.q: What happens if Google rate-limits the run?
faq.a: The actor waits 5 seconds, then 20. If the engine keeps answering 429, or answers 401/403 once, that engine stops for the rest of the run and its remaining rows come back as rate-limited, free. Re-run later to fill them in.
